NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING AND AGENDA
NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS
Tuesday, May 10, 2022
ONE OR MORE SUPERVISORS MAY ATTEND VIA VIDEO AND/OR TELEPHONICALLY 
The Navajo County Board of Supervisors will hold a meeting open to the public on Tuesday, May 10, 2022, in the Supervisors’
Chamber in the Navajo County Governmental Complex, 100 East Code Talkers Drive, Holbrook, Arizona. The Board may vote to
meet in a closed executive session to discuss certain matters and for legal advice on any item as indicated on the following
agenda, pursuant to A.R.S. § 38-431.03(A) (3). 
The Navajo County Board of Supervisors finds that it is in the best interest of the Community to conduct this public meeting using
a hybrid method in order to serve the public interest. Board members will participate in the meeting, in-person in the Board
of Supervisors Chambers in Holbrook, or via Zoom. Limited seating will be available for the public.
To Join Zoom Meeting now, click here: 
https://us06web.zoom.us/j/84264615494?pwd=a3ZVWS9YWUpSV1BOWDRvUVVNbHFyZz09
Web Conference:
Call In Number: 1-346-248-7799 OR 1-669-900-6833 (you may use either teleconference number)
Meeting ID: 842 6461 5494
Passcode: 945459
If you would like to speak during Call to the Public please take the following actions:
1. Email Melissa Buckley at, melissa.buckley@navajocountyaz.gov
2. Identify the Board of Supervisors' meeting date, the agenda item # and title.
3. Name & Telephone Number
4. Comments or questions should be sent by 5:00 pm. the day prior to the Board meeting.
Persons with disabilities who need accommodation to attend or participate in the meeting may contact the Clerk of the Board’s office
at (928) 524-4053; at least 48 hours prior to the meeting, so an accommodation can be arranged.
Items on the agenda may be considered out of order at the Chairman’s discretion. A copy of the agenda background material
provided to the Board, except items to be considered in executive session, is available for public inspection at Navajo County
website, www.navajocountyaz.gov
“NOTICE TO PARENTS AND LEGAL GUARDIANS: Parents and legal guardians have the right to consent before Navajo County makes a video or
voice recording of a minor child, pursuant to A.R.S. § 1-602(A)(9). The Navajo County Board of Supervisors regular meetings are recorded and may
be viewed on Navajo County’s website, and social media pages. If you permit your child to attend/participate in a televised Navajo County Board of
Supervisors meeting, a recording will be made, and your child’s picture may be posted on Navajo County’s social media pages. You may exercise
your right not to consent by not allowing your child to attend/participate in the meeting.” 
9:00 a.m. Call To Order: Invocation and Pledge of Allegiance
           
1. CALL TO THE PUBLIC: Individuals may address the Board on any relevant issue for up to
5 minutes. At the close of the call to the public, Board members may not respond to any
comments but may respond to criticism, ask staff to review a matter or ask that a matter be
placed on a future agenda.
 
 
2. CONSENT AGENDA: These items are considered to be routine or administrative in nature
and will be approved in a single motion. A Board member may request for any item to be
removed from the consent agenda and considered on the regular agenda:
 
 
a. Minutes: April 26, 2022, Regular Meeting and May 5, 2022, Emergency Meeting  
 
b. Constable Reports: Show Low Precinct #5 and Pinetop-Lakeside Precinct #6, April 2022  
 
c. Sympathy Letter to: Amber Stafford (Health Department)

<!-- page 2 -->
d. Warrant & Voucher Report over $1000, April 2022  
 
e. Two year appointment for Bonnie Secakuku to serve on the Navajo County Extension
Advisory Board
 
 
f. Fiscal Year 2021/2022 Fund Transfers  
 
g. Letter of Agency Addendum for the Sparklight Contract at the Winslow Complex  
 
h. Tax exemptions filed pursuant to ARS §42-11153 as a Request for Redemption of Waiver  
 
i. National Forest Funds Distribution $907,510.61 for the benefit of Public Schools and Public
Roads pursuant to A.R.S. §11-497, A.R.S. §37-741 and A.R.S. §37-521
 
 
j. Forest Fee Distribution amounts for School Districts  
 
k. Special Event Liquor License to 180th Field Artillery Regiment Association for a music and
camping event over Memorial Day Weekend to be held at 4 Silos @ GreatSky Camp Ranch,
7863 White Mountain Lake Road, Show Low
 
 
l. Special Event Liquor License to Heber-Overgaard Chamber of Commerce for their annual 4th
of July activities to be held at the Tall Timbers Park in Heber-Overgaard
 
 
m. Conduct Elections for the City of Show Low, City of Holbrook, Town of Pinetop-Lakeside,
Town of Snowflake and the Town of Taylor on August 2, 2022, and the City of Winslow on
November 8, 2022
 
 
3. BOARD OF SUPERVISORS:  
 
a. Recognition of those who contributed to County Health Week for their hard work and
dedication to make all of the events a success through the different communities in Navajo
County.
 
Presented By: Vice-Chairman Alberto Peshlakai
 
4. ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES:  
 
a. Presentation to Bonita Chase on her Retirement from Navajo County after 21+ Years of Service  
Presented By: Eric Scott and Kirsti Hancock
 
b. Consideration of a grant agreement between Navajo County and Chilchinbeto Chapter.  
Presented By: Ken Maruyama
 
c. Consideration of a grant agreement between Navajo County and the City of Show Low.  
Presented By: Ken Maruyama
 
5. PUBLIC WORKS:  
 
a. Consideration of a Proclamation declaring the week of May 15-21, 2022 as National Public

<!-- page 3 -->
a. Consideration of a Proclamation declaring the week of May 15-21, 2022 as National Public
Works Week in Navajo County.
 
Presented By: John Osgood
 
b. VICTORY HEIGHTS ROAD MAINTENANCE DISTRICT: Board of Directors Session:  
 
1. CONSENT AGENDA: The following item(s) are considered to be of a routine or
administrative in nature and will be approved as a group unless a member of the Board wishes
to discuss a particular item: 
 
 
a. Appointment of Jeff Baker to the Victory Heights Road Maintenance District Advisory
Committee
 
 
6. WHITE MOUNTAIN LAKES COUNTY RECREATION IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT:
Board of Directors Session:
 
 
a. CONSENT AGENDA: The following item(s) are considered to be of a routine or
administrative in nature and will be approved as a group unless a member of the Board wishes
to discuss a particular item: 
 
 
1. Amendment No. 2, extending the Professional Services Agreement with Remarkable
Recreation Solutions for one additional year, May 26, 2022 through May 25, 2023.
 
 
7. COUNTY BUSINESS UPDATE: Report from County Manager, County Attorney and Board
members.
 
 
 
8. ADJOURN  
 
Dated: NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 
Posted:________ By:_____                         
Melissa W. Buckley - Clerk of the Board

§42-11153, “If a widow, widower or disabled person whose property is exempt from tax under section §42-1111, the

Motion before the Board:

Background:
The Navajo County Board of Supervisors approved ARPA funded projects at the January 25th
meeting. Chilchinbeto Chapter was successful in obtaining $200,000 from the County's ARPA
grant funds. In order to ensure successful implementation of the grant, Navajo County and
Chilchinbeto Chapter enter into an agreement. The grant's terms and conditions enable county
staff to monitor and report the project's progress and success.

Appendix I 
 
Grant # 
• #055 
 
Title 
• Chilchinbeto Sewer Expansion 
 
Point of Contact 
• Eugene Badonie 
• 928-697-5681 
• ebadonie@navajochapters.org 
 
Description 
• Chilchinbeto, a Navajo Nation Chapter, proposes development of a lagoon and sewage lines in 
the community.  
• The project will enhance tourism, local economy, and community health.  
• The total project cost is estimated at $1,500,000. Navajo County provides up to $200,000 from 
the County’s ARPA funds.  
 
Deliverables 
• Complete the Project Activity, Timeline, and Expenditure Summary Sheet (see below), and 
update the sheet every quarter.  
• Submit project progress reports every quarter (see Appendix II).  
• Provide the project’s supporting documents as available.  
• Request reimbursements of the project’s costs with proof of payment.  
• Respond to the County’s inquiries about the project in a timely manner.  
• Obligate the funding by the end of September 2024.  
• Complete the proposed project by the end of September 2026. 
• Celebrate the project’s milestones (e.g. groundbreaking and opening events) with county officials.  
 
Timeline 
• A timetable for quarterly project progress reports is provided in Appendix II.  
• The fund should be obligated by the end of September 2024.  
• The project should be completed by the end of September 2026.  
 
Acknowledgement 
• Please acknowledge the work on this grant from Navajo County as follows: “This work was 
supported by Navajo County ARPA Grant Program.”  
 
Supporting Documents 
• Project application. 
• Project planning and marketing documents. 
• Project milestone and completion documents. 
• Proof of payments.  
• Other documents relevant to the project.

STAFF SUMMARY REPORT 
 
AGENDA TITLE: Consideration of Acceptance of American R escue Plan Act Funds from 
Navajo County (Justin Johnson) 
 
 
 
I MOVE to authorize the acceptance of $200,000.00 in American Rescue Plan Act funds from 
Navajo County and authorize the Mayor to sign the associated agreement. 
 
 
 
In 2021, Navajo County officials asked all cities and towns in the County to submit a list of 
American R escue Plan Act (ARPA) eligible projects to Navajo County for consideration. On 
September 16, 2021, City staff applied to Navajo County requesting funding for several ARPA 
eligible projects.  On January 26, 2022, staff was notified that the County Board of Supervisors 
approved $200,000.00 in ARPA funds  for the Frontier P ark Inclusive P layground and 
Splashpad. 
 
Staff recommends accepting the funds and authorizing the Mayor to sign the agreement 
 
Once the ag reement is signed , staff will submit  the agreement and other required documents 
to the County for review and approval.

Description 
• The City has plans to construct an all-inclusive, ADA playground and splash pad that will provide 
outdoor activity space for children of all ages regardless of their physical and cognitive abilities. 
The playground will be constructed at Frontier Field on 9th Place in downtown Show Low.  
• The playground will provide outdoor exercise opportunities where social distancing can be 
maintained.  
• The total project cost is estimated at $2 million. Navajo County provides partial funding (up to 
$200,000) from the ARPA funds.  
 
Deliverables 
• Complete the Project Activity, Timeline, and Expenditure Summary Sheet (see below), and 
update the sheet every quarter.  
• Submit project progress reports every quarter (see Appendix II).  
• Provide the project’s supporting documents as available.  
• Request reimbursements of the project’s costs with proof of payment.  
• Respond to the County’s inquiries about the project in a timely manner.  
• Obligate the funding by the end of September 2024.  
• Complete the proposed project by the end of September 2026. 
• Celebrate the project’s milestones (e.g. groundbreaking and opening events) with county officials.  
 
Timeline 
• A timetable for quarterly project progress reports is provided in Appendix II.  
• The fund should be obligated by the end of September 2024.  
• The project should be completed by the end of September 2026.  
 
Acknowledgement 
• Please acknowledge the work on this grant from Navajo County as follows: “This work was 
supported by Navajo County ARPA Grant Program.”  
 
Supporting Documents 
• Project application. 
• Project planning and marketing documents. 
• Project milestone and completion documents. 
• Proof of payments.  
• Other documents relevant to the project.

Board of Supervisors Regular 5. a.        
Meeting Date: 05/10/2022  
Title: Proclamation Declaring the Week of May 15-21 as National Public Works Week in
Navajo County
Submitted For: John Osgood, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: John Osgood, Public Works Director
Department: Public Works
Presented By: John Osgood
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of a Proclamation declaring the week of May 15-21, 2022 as National Public
Works Week in Navajo County.
Background:
The American Public Works Association has sponsored National Public Works Week since
1960.  Communities throughout North America use this week to remind the public of the
importance of public works in their daily lives.  This year's theme is "Ready and Resilient," which
reflects the commitment of the County's Public Works and Emergency Management teams to
prepare for and rebound from weather and non-weather related events in service to the public. For
Navajo County, vital Public Works, Emergency Management and Facility Maintenance
operations and services include: 
Roadway maintenance and snow removal operations
Tribal transportation project and community cleanup coordination
Administrative business and governmental finance services
Facility maintenance and custodial operations
Emergency Management Coordination
Technical engineering and flood control services
Planning and development services
Fleet maintenance operations 
In addition to educating and reminding the public about the importance of public works services,
recognition of National Public Works Week in Navajo County offers the opportunity to thank and
acknowledge the outstanding work of the men and women of our Public Works, Emergency
Management and Facility Maintenance work teams .  Not only do they provide daily professional
public works services which protect the health and safety and enhance the quality of life of Navajo
County residents, businesses and visitors, many of our employees are emergency responders
during snow storms, fires, floods, traffic accidents and other public safety incidents.  Given the
outstanding contributions our employees make in protecting our health, safety, quality of life and
essential built infrastructure, all the people of Navajo County are encouraged to join with
representatives of the American Public Works Association in recognizing the important efforts of
the men and women of the Navajo County Public Works, Health and Facility Maintenance
Departments.

Navajo County               
Proclamation 
National Public Works Week 
May 15–21, 2022 
“Ready and Resilient” 
WHEREAS, public works professionals focus on infrastructure, facilities and services that are of vital importance to 
sustainable and resilient communities and to the public health, high quality of life and well-being of the people of Navajo 
County; and 
WHEREAS, these infrastructure projects, maintenance operations, emergency management coordination and essential 
services could not be provided without the dedicated effo rts of public works professionals from state and local 
governments and the private sector; and 
WHEREAS, the men and women of  the Navajo County Public Works, Emergency Management and Facility Maintenance 
teams excel in protecting our infrastructure and the  health and safety of residents, businesses, and visitors by expertly 
providing roadway maintenance and snow removal operations; administrative business and governmental finance 
services; facility maintenance and custodial operations; emergency management coordination; technical engineering and 
flood control services; planning and development services ; tribal transportation project and community cleanup 
coordination; and fleet maintenance operations;  and  
WHEREAS, many of our employees are emergency responders 24/7 during snowstorms, fires, floods, traffic accidents and 
other public safety incidents; and 
WHEREAS, these dedicated employees strive to embody the Navajo County values of Teamwork, Accountability, Integrity, 
Excellence, and Innovation every day while providing superior public service.  
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT PROCLAIMED, by the Board of Supervisors of Navajo County, that May 15-21, 2022 is 
designated as “National Public Works Week” in our community and urge all the people of Navajo County to join with 
representatives of the American Public Works Association to thank the men and women of Navajo County Public Works, 
Emergency Management and Facility Maintenance for the outstanding contributions they make in protecting our health, 
safety, and quality of life.  
 
PASSED, ADOPTED AND APPROVED by the Board of Supervisors on May 10, 2022.
